subject: Model fit & safety follow-up — HealthScope
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Parker <emily.parker@healthscope.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: model fit & safety (post-discovery)

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of needs we heard: 
- Assist clinicians with triage guidance and administrative summarization; NOT providing definitive medical diagnoses.
- High refusal/deflection fidelity on sensitive or clinical-diagnostic prompts.
- Low latency for patient-facing flows (target P95 < 600ms).
- SOC2 + procurement checklist required for pilots.

Recommended immediate steps: 
1) We'll run a model-fit sweep on your sample transcripts (thanks for offering those) with our safety/refusal evals.
2) Deliver: short report with recommended model + prompt templates, benchmark links, and expected refusal/false-accept rates.
3) If results look good, propose a 2-week pilot on Dedicated or Private deployment depending on your requirements.

Model candidates we plan to evaluate (initial): 
- redwood-3b-int8 (cost-efficient; good summarization)
- redwood-7b-q4 (best balance of latency/quality for triage)
- redwood-14b-guard (higher-quality, stronger refusal baseline)

Safety & eval focus: refusal consistency on clinical-diagnostic prompts, hallucination rate on medication/regimen questions, and policy-behavior on sensitive PHI-related requests. We'll include concrete guardrail prompt recipes (explicit refusal templates + escalation handoffs).

Can you confirm the following so we can start the sweep? 
- Share sample transcripts S3/Drive link (or permission to download the zip).
- Any additional policies for allowed escalation (e.g., handoff to clinician vs. provide educational info).
- SLA targets for latency and refusal/false-accept thresholds (if you have internal KPIs).

If that works I'll have Dylan kick off the evals once we have sample data/access. Deliverables: model_fit_report.pdf and safety-evals-summary.csv within ~3 business days of us receiving the samples.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposal-one-pager.pdf (PDF)]

From: Emily Parker <emily.parker@healthscope.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@healthscope.com, Dr. Rajiv Singh <r.singh@healthscope.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & safety (post-discovery)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear notes. Confirming we're interested in a pilot focused on triage and admin summarization. I uploaded a redacted sample set here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XYZ_healthscope_samples (password-protected zip).

A few clarifications from our side: 
- Procurement loop: procurement@healthscope.com is on CC — they'll need SOC2 docs and a statement of work / rough pricing.
- Safety KPI: our clinical governance team prefers refusal precision > 95% on clinical-diagnostic prompts (the product team is flexible on recall).
- On-prem question: we may need a private deployment option due to PHI; would like an estimate for Private deployment and timeline.

Can you also include a short demo of the guardrail prompts during the next call? We're available Mon or Tue morning next week.

Thanks,
Emily
Head of Product, Clinical Tools
HealthScope

[Attachment: healthscope_sample_transcripts.zip (ZIP)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Parker <emily.parker@healthscope.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & safety (post-discovery)

Perfect — thanks for the upload and procurement heads-up. We'll start the sweep today. Initial notes / commitments: 

- Deliverables (within ~3 business days): model_fit_report.pdf, safety-evals-summary.csv, and a short recording of guardrail demos.
- Baseline internal evals (on workloads similar to yours) show refusal precision ~96–98% on direct clinical-diagnostic asks for redwood-14b-guard, with hallucination rates < 2% for medication mentions. We'll validate on your exact transcripts and produce per-prompt metrics.
- Guardrail recipes we'll test: explicit refusal template, stepwise de-escalation (provide high-level info + immediate handoff), and structured escalation payloads for clinician review.

Attachments I'm including as stubs for reference: [Attachment: model_fit_report.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: safety-evals-summary.csv (CSV)]. These are work-in-progress and will be refreshed after we run your samples.

Dylan will reach out for S3 credentials or Drive access if needed. We can run the evals in Private if PHI requires it — cost and lead time estimates will come back in the SOW.

Best,
Marissa

> On Thu, Mar 12, 2026 at 10:02 AM, Emily Parker <emily.parker@healthscope.com> wrote:
> > I uploaded a redacted sample set here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XYZ_healthscope_samples
> > procurement@healthscope.com is on CC — they'll need SOC2 docs and SOW/pricing.

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Parker <emily.parker@healthscope.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & safety (post-discovery)

Hi all —

Quick technical plan from our side so expectations are clear: 
- Evaluation metrics: refusal_precision, refusal_consistency (same prompt -> same refusal behavior), hallucination_rate (factuality on meds/regimen), summary_ROUGE/ROUGE-L for administrative outputs, latency P50/P95.
- Prompt sets: we'll run three variants — baseline (no guardrails), soft-guard (instruction + refusal template), hard-guard (instruction + strict disallowed topics list + forced refusal).
- Sampling & privacy: we'll run everything in an isolated Private env if you prefer; otherwise we can run on Hosted with your signed DPA + limited retention.
- Timeline: 3 business days to get initial sweep report after we have access; deeper per-prompt regression evals ~5 business days.

Needed from HealthScope to proceed: S3 link or Drive access to the zip (the link Emily shared looks good) and any redaction/PHI rules to apply. Also, if procurement prefers an NDA before we process samples, let us know and Marissa can coordinate.

I'll provision the eval cluster and kick off the runs once we confirm access.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Principal ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Parker <emily.parker@healthscope.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@healthscope.com, Dr. Rajiv Singh <r.singh@healthscope.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & safety (post-discovery)

Marissa / Dylan —

Thanks — this looks good. Procurement: we'd like an SOW and ballpark pricing for a 2-week pilot (include Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private price ranges). Our procurement contact is procurement@healthscope.com.

A couple more asks: 
- Can you include a short SLA note for refusal/false-accept behavior? Even a non-binding target will help our clinical governance review.
- Please confirm whether Private deployment requires on-prem hardware vs. VPC-hosted customer-managed options.

Deal id for our internal tracking: HS-2026-045. Happy to schedule a demo of the guardrail prompts on Monday 3/16 at 10am PT.

Best,
Emily

[Attachment: procurement-checklist.pdf (PDF)]
